methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates WGS (100x), scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, functional lentiviral reconstitution in K562/JJN3, flow cytometry, confocal imaging, cytotoxicity assays, and AlphaFold2 structural modeling across a 21-patient multi-institutional talquetamab-relapse cohort, with pre/post paired samples in 8 patients and matched germline in 19/21 — a mismatched normal (NA12878) handled with panel-of-normals and gnomAD filtering for MM-62/MM-63. The authors explicitly state no sample-size calculation was performed given restricted primary material and that primary-sample functional experiments were run once, while cell-line experiments were triplicate biological replicates; this is a clear and transparently acknowledged limitation that caps rigor below 5. Statistical handling is appropriate: dose–response IC50 with 95% CI from profile-likelihood, two-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD multiplicity correction, dNdScv for positive selection (q_global_cv < 1e-5), GISTIC2 for recurrent CNA, and CCF/clonality via ASCAT, Palimpsest, and FACETS. Weaknesses include single-replicate primary-sample assays, no explicit multiple-testing correction across the broader genomic survey beyond dNdScv, and no formal power analysis for the 68.4% escape-rate estimate (CI not reported for the proportion).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design is a multi-institutional retrospective correlative case series (n=21) of post-talquetamab relapses paired with mechanistic preclinical validation; this maps to Oxford CEBM level 4 (case series/low-quality cohort), with the functional cell-line and structural work at level 5. Clinical relevance is high: the paper directly explains clinical resistance to an FDA-approved TCE (talquetamab), identifies genomic/epitope mutations (e.g., p.Asp239Asn) with dose-dependent impact on talquetamab vs forimtamig, provides a biologic rationale for bivalent/biparatopic/multi-antigen designs, and warns against sub-therapeutic dosing and reliance on antibody-based screening when SNVs preserve epitope-independent surface expression. Endpoints are patient-relevant (PFS, IMWG response) and the mechanistic findings have near-term translational utility for patient stratification and next-generation TCE engineering.

reporting_quality.justification: The study is a hybrid translational report; ARRIVE-adjacent reporting is most applicable for the preclinical core, with STROBE elements for the observational cohort. Methods are thorough: ethics IDs, trial identifiers (NCT04108195, NCT04634552), antibody tables, software versions, cell-line authentication (CLASTR), and detailed pipelines are provided; a Nature Reporting Summary is referenced. Gaps include no CONSORT/STROBE flow diagram, limited patient demographic reporting outside Supplementary Table 1, and single-run primary-sample assays. Data availability is partially discernible — prior data are deposited at GEO (GSE199373/GSE199268/GSE199359), but new WGS/scRNA/scATAC accession numbers and code repositories are REDACTED in the blinded text; cell lines and plasmids are 'available upon reasonable request,' consistent with a mid-range reproducibility posture.

novelty_literature.justification: Prior work (refs 13, 16, 19, 20) established biallelic GPRC5D deletions and epigenetic silencing as escape mechanisms after anti-GPRC5D CAR T or TCE in small series (n≤8). This study substantially extends the field by (1) assembling the largest post-talquetamab cohort to date (n=21) with integrated WGS+scRNA+scATAC, (2) establishing SNVs/indels — including convergent subclonal mutations clustering in GPCR-family-conserved ER-to-membrane trafficking motifs — as a dominant and previously under-recognized mechanism, (3) functionally dissecting ER-trapping vs epitope-binding loss, and (4) demonstrating differential vulnerability of mutants to monovalent (talquetamab) vs bivalent (forimtamig) TCEs with structural rationale (PDB 9IMA + AlphaFold2). Not first-in-class, but a meaningful mechanistic and translational advance beyond incremental confirmation.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear narrative arc from clinical cohort → genomic mechanisms → functional validation → structural modeling → translational implications. Figure captions are detailed and standalone-interpretable, acronyms are generally expanded, and the Discussion synthesizes the three resistance patterns without rehashing results. Minor issues: Fig. 6d caption has a truncated 'n = for each cell line'; some sentences in the SNV subsections are dense with per-patient variant lists that would benefit from a summary table in the main text; the Abstract conveys the key numeric findings (68.4%, three mechanisms) and mechanistic logic effectively.

key_strengths: Largest reported post-talquetamab multi-institutional cohort (n=21) with integrated WGS + scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq and paired pre/post samples
Identifies three convergent resistance mechanisms including a previously under-appreciated class of GPRC5D SNVs/indels clustering in GPCR-conserved ER-to-membrane trafficking motifs
Rigorous functional validation (K562/JJN3 reconstitution, confocal ER-colocalization, dose-response cytotoxicity) linking specific mutants to differential monovalent vs bivalent TCE sensitivity
Structural rationale via cryo-EM template (PDB 9IMA) and AlphaFold2 Multimer for p.Asp239Asn epitope disruption and p.Tyr257Ser trafficking defect
Clear translational implications: argues against sub-therapeutic dosing, supports multivalent/biparatopic and dual-antigen strategies, warns against relying on antibody-based screening alone
key_concerns: Primary-sample functional assays conducted only once (acknowledged, but limits inference for individual-patient claims)
No formal sample-size justification or confidence interval reported for the 68.4% GPRC5D-escape proportion
Two WGS cases (MM-62, MM-63) rely on a mismatched NA12878 germline control; residual germline contamination risk is only partially mitigated
Data/code accession numbers and availability statements are REDACTED in the blinded text, limiting independent reproducibility verification
T-cell-fitness analyses in antigen-retained relapses (n=2 durable remissions) are underpowered to establish antigen-independent resistance as a parallel mechanism
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mechanistically rich, clinically actionable, multi-omic + functional + structural study on resistance to an approved TCE in myeloma. The scope, novelty beyond prior small series, and immediate translational implications place it at the top tier (Nature Medicine / Cancer Cell / Nature Cancer); residual single-replicate primary-sample work and reporting gaps warrant minor revisions rather than acceptance.
